facts.f: India has 28 states and 8 union territories (since 2020).
facts.e: States have their own elected governments. Union territories are run more directly by the central government.

facts.f: New Delhi is the capital of India.
facts.e: It was officially inaugurated as the capital in 1931. Earlier, Calcutta (now Kolkata) was the capital of British India, until the move to Delhi was announced in 1911.

facts.f: Rajasthan is India's largest state by area.
facts.e: Much of the Thar Desert lies in Rajasthan.

facts.f: Goa is India's smallest state by area.
facts.e: It is famous for its beaches along the Arabian Sea.

facts.f: Uttar Pradesh has more people than any other Indian state.
facts.e: This was shown by the 2011 Census.

facts.f: India's national anthem, 'Jana Gana Mana', was written by Rabindranath Tagore.
facts.e: It was adopted as the national anthem on 24 January 1950. Singing the full anthem takes about 52 seconds.

facts.f: India's national song is 'Vande Mataram', written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.
facts.e: It inspired many freedom fighters.

facts.f: The Indian flag has saffron, white and green stripes, with a navy-blue wheel in the middle.
facts.e: The wheel is the Ashoka Chakra, which has 24 spokes.

facts.f: India's national flag is based on a design by Pingali Venkayya.
facts.e: The flag was adopted on 22 July 1947.

facts.f: India's national emblem comes from the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath.
facts.e: Below it is written 'Satyameva Jayate', meaning 'Truth alone triumphs'.

facts.f: The rupee symbol ₹ was adopted in 2010. It was designed by D. Udaya Kumar.
facts.e: It blends the Devanagari letter 'र' (ra) and the Roman letter 'R'.

facts.f: The Ganga is India's national river.
facts.e: It flows from the Gangotri Glacier in the Himalayas to the Bay of Bengal.

facts.f: The mango is India's national fruit.
facts.e: India grows more mangoes than any other country.

facts.f: India has not officially named any sport as its national game.
facts.e: Hockey is often called the national game because of India's great Olympic record in it.

facts.f: India became independent on 15 August 1947.
facts.e: Every year, the Prime Minister hoists the flag at the Red Fort in Delhi on Independence Day.

facts.f: India became a republic on 26 January 1950, when the Constitution came into force.
facts.e: We celebrate this day as Republic Day, with a grand parade in New Delhi.

facts.f: The Ganga is the longest river flowing within India.
facts.e: It travels about 2,500 km through India.

facts.f: The Thar Desert, also called the Great Indian Desert, lies mostly in Rajasthan.
facts.e: Camels are used to cross its sand dunes.

facts.f: The Taj Mahal in Agra was built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
facts.e: It is made of white marble and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

facts.f: Indian Standard Time is based on the 82.5° East line of longitude.
facts.e: This line passes near Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh.

facts.f: The Eighth Schedule of India's Constitution lists 22 languages.
facts.e: They include Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Urdu and Sanskrit.

facts.f: Hindi in Devanagari script is the official language of India's central government.
facts.e: English is also used for official work.

facts.f: Bharatanatyam comes from Tamil Nadu and Kathakali from Kerala.
facts.e: Other classical dances include Kathak, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

facts.f: Diwali is the festival of lights and Holi is the festival of colours.
facts.e: Pongal in Tamil Nadu, Onam in Kerala and Bihu in Assam are harvest festivals.

facts.f: The Sundarbans is home to the Royal Bengal tiger.
facts.e: Tigers there are good swimmers and live among the mangroves.

facts.f: The Indus Valley Civilisation was one of the world's oldest civilisations.
facts.e: Its planned cities included Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Dholavira and Lothal.

facts.f: Chess is believed to have started in India as a game called chaturanga.
facts.e: Chaturanga had pieces for the four parts of an army: infantry, cavalry, elephants and chariots.

facts.f: Yoga began in ancient India. International Yoga Day is on 21 June.
facts.e: 21 June is usually the longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere.

facts.f: The Western Ghats is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
facts.e: These mountains have a huge variety of plants and animals found nowhere else.

facts.f: Indian Railways runs one of the largest railway networks in the world.
facts.e: Millions of people travel on its trains every day.

facts.f: The Statue of Unity in Gujarat is 182 metres tall.
facts.e: It honours Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. When it opened in 2018 it was the tallest statue in the world.

facts.f: Lakshadweep is India's smallest union territory, and Ladakh is the largest.
facts.e: Lakshadweep is a group of coral islands. Ladakh is a high, cold desert.

facts.f: Mumbai is the capital of Maharashtra, Chennai of Tamil Nadu and Kolkata of West Bengal.
facts.e: These three cities are also big ports.

facts.f: Bengaluru is the capital of Karnataka, Hyderabad of Telangana and Thiruvananthapuram of Kerala.
facts.e: Bengaluru is often called India's Silicon Valley because of its technology companies.

facts.f: Jaipur is the capital of Rajasthan, Lucknow of Uttar Pradesh and Patna of Bihar.
facts.e: Jaipur is known as the Pink City.

facts.f: Bhopal is the capital of Madhya Pradesh, and Gandhinagar is the capital of Gujarat.
facts.e: Gandhinagar is named after Mahatma Gandhi.

facts.f: Chandigarh is the capital of both Punjab and Haryana.
facts.e: It is also a union territory. It was planned by the architect Le Corbusier.

facts.f: Dispur is the capital of Assam and Shillong is the capital of Meghalaya.
facts.e: Shillong is sometimes called the 'Scotland of the East'.

facts.f: Gangtok is the capital of Sikkim, Imphal of Manipur and Kohima of Nagaland.
facts.e: These are hill cities in north-eastern India.

facts.f: Bhubaneswar is the capital of Odisha and Ranchi is the capital of Jharkhand.
facts.e: Bhubaneswar is known as the Temple City of India.

facts.f: Sikkim became India's first fully organic state in 2016.
facts.e: Its farms grow crops without chemical fertilisers or pesticides.

facts.f: Nalanda in Bihar was a famous ancient centre of learning.
facts.e: Students came from many countries to study there. Its ruins are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

facts.f: The Tropic of Cancer passes through eight Indian states.
facts.e: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

facts.f: The Konark Sun Temple in Odisha is built like a giant stone chariot.
facts.e: It has 24 carved stone wheels pulled by stone horses.

facts.f: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first Prime Minister and Dr Rajendra Prasad was the first President.
facts.e: Dr Rajendra Prasad was President for 12 years, longer than anyone since.

facts.f: India's national calendar is the Saka calendar.
facts.e: It is used alongside the Gregorian calendar for official purposes.
